direction.name: Editorial and considered
direction.intent: Make the central idea memorable through typographic contrast and deliberate sequencing, without delaying the next useful action.

composition.focal: Give one outcome-led headline the largest scale; pair it with one relevant artifact or service detail, not competing feature tiles.
sequence: Introduce the outcome and primary action, then show concrete offerings, practical details and the next step.
composition.grouping: Align content to a shared text edge; use an asymmetric feature beside a narrower practical-information rail.
composition.density: Give the opening breathing room, then tighten repeated offerings; do not leave empty grid cells at the end of a section.
composition.responsive: On narrow screens place title, practical facts and primary action before optional imagery; turn the information rail into a compact inline block.

typography.display: Preserve the existing brand/design-system faces; express this direction through hierarchy, spacing and weight instead of replacing fonts.
typography.body: Keep prose near 45–75 characters per line; use a readable local body face and at least 1.45 line height for paragraphs.
typography.scale: Use one clearly dominant display step, a distinct section step and restrained labels; reduce display size before it crowds narrow actions.
typography.numerals: Use tabular lining numbers for comparisons, align units consistently, and keep identifiers distinct from prose.

color.foundation: Bind foundation and foreground to the existing brand/design-system tokens; keep their established identity.
color.accent: Use the existing action/selection accent with restraint; do not replace the palette to match this direction.
color.semantic: Reserve success, warning and danger for labeled states; never use brand color alone to communicate a result.
color.surfaces: Use the page foundation, one working surface and one meaningful divider before adding shadows or nested frames.
color.dark: In dark environments use raised surfaces and quieter accents; recheck text, control and focus contrast instead of inverting colors.
color.contrast: Verify chosen rendered pairs: ordinary text 4.5:1, large text 3:1, meaningful UI/focus boundaries 3:1 where required; inspect exceptions.

trust: State what an action really does, its scope and whether data is saved locally or sent; acknowledge completion without fabricated claims.
Use real product evidence only; never invent endorsements, customer counts, certifications, security guarantees or scarcity.
avoid: Avoid repeating identical rounded cards for every section; let content importance determine its scale and boundary.
Avoid oversized headlines that hide practical facts or force users to scroll to the only useful action.

selection.basis: Explicit character preference: editorial; this does not override brand or required constraints.

binding.color: Reuse existing brand color roles; no replacement palette is authorized.
binding.typography: Reuse the brand fonts; no remote/proprietary font requirement.
binding.density: Give the opening breathing room, then tighten repeated offerings; do not leave empty grid cells at the end of a section.

motion.name: Action confirmation
motion.when: Use only when an evidenced feedback interaction needs feedback or continuity; optional motion is not a product requirement.
motion.problem: A user must know whether an action succeeded, failed or only changed local state.
motion.animate: Transition a small acknowledgement or checkmark after the real result; pair it with a persistent status message.
motion.stable: Keep the action label area and content position stable; do not move focus into a toast.
motion.easing: Prefer ease-out for arrivals; ease-in for departures; keep direct manipulation immediate.
motion.accessibility: Keep keyboard focus visible and semantics/live feedback independent of animation; essential actions must remain immediately usable.
motion.reducedMotion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, remove spatial movement and looping effects; retain an instant state change and textual feedback.
motion.performance: Prefer opacity/transform on small elements; avoid per-frame layout, large blur/repaint regions and permanent will-change hints.
motion.avoid: Avoid fake success, automatic dismissal of critical errors and delaying the action until an effect finishes.

motion.name: Hover and press feedback
motion.when: Use only when an evidenced press interaction needs feedback or continuity; optional motion is not a product requirement.
motion.problem: Communicate which choice or control is being activated without moving its neighbors.
motion.animate: Use a small opacity or bounded press transform; communicate selection with a stable border and explicit selected state.
motion.stable: Keep control dimensions, selected label and hit area stable; hover must not be the only state cue.
motion.easing: Prefer ease-out for arrivals; ease-in for departures; keep direct manipulation immediate.
motion.accessibility: Keep keyboard focus visible and semantics/live feedback independent of animation; essential actions must remain immediately usable.
motion.reducedMotion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, remove spatial movement and looping effects; retain an instant state change and textual feedback.
motion.performance: Prefer opacity/transform on small elements; avoid per-frame layout, large blur/repaint regions and permanent will-change hints.
motion.avoid: Avoid bouncing buttons, hover-only controls and scale effects that crop focus outlines.

limits: Inspect stable DIR/MOT/QUA IDs for detail. Use existing recommend 2.1 plus targeted inspection for eligible component/composition contracts.
No beauty, emotion or user-trust score is computed. Review indicators require rendered evidence and contextual human/agent judgment.
Motion is optional, task/interaction-gated and limited to two full records. Query matches are discovery hints, not applicability evidence.
English declared terms and adjacent negation only; inferred task/context values do not become observed facts.
